open_points.subject: Attempt-number assignment for files spooled before a NodeExecution
open_points.text: “`store` alone assigns `attempt_number` ... no caller passes a number” but “the spooling module reads [the next ordinal] as the count of the element's NodeExecutions plus one”
open_points.question: Who computes and communicates the tentative attempt number used in a SpooledFile before its NodeExecution exists?
options: `store.spool_file` computes and returns the next ordinal, which callers treat as opaque
The spooling module computes count-plus-one and passes it to `store`
`store` first reserves an attempt identifier that subsequent spool and record calls use
open_points.default_guess: Have `store.spool_file` compute and return the next ordinal; callers echo only the returned SpooledFile reference and never calculate an attempt number.

open_points.subject: Logical availability of spooled-file bytes after run end or release
open_points.text: “`read_value_bytes` ... A spooled file whose run no longer holds its spool is refused” while `store` “Must not own ... when a run's spool is emptied or released (that is `runs`)”
open_points.question: Which module decides that a spooled file is logically unavailable when removal failed or was interrupted and its bytes still physically exist?
options: `runs` exposes a capability that checks run state and gates the byte read
`store` interprets Run status and release fields despite their ownership by `runs`
A store-owned availability marker is changed atomically with the run record
open_points.default_guess: Make `runs` own the logical eligibility check and expose the gated spooled-file read; `store` should only perform the physical byte access.
